description: B-flood is a flood solver built as a subset of the Basilisk software, with a public archive deposited by Geoffroy Kirstetter and Stephane Popinet. It solves the Saint-Venant shallow-water equations with adaptive mesh refinement for flash-flood applications. The own documentation links analytical tests, Toce valley examples and a Karamea River tutorial. Spatial coverage and resolution follow the configured watershed and adaptive mesh, not a fixed observation grid. Source and example access are free, and the B-flood archive metadata declares CC-BY-4.0; Basilisk must be installed separately and retains its own terms. The code can support flood-hazard and emergency-planning simulations around buildings and drainage systems. A limitation is that the Cannes 2015 case cannot be fully reproduced from the public package because the authors cannot redistribute its IGN terrain and Meteo-France files. Other published tests remain available for reuse. The solver runs within Basilisk, and no simulation was executed or archive downloaded.
